error_note: A low glucose on a lactose tolerance test means a flat rise (lactase deficiency), not hypoglycemia; hypoglycemia is also shared by 207 diseases and is not a characteristic feature of D-glyceric aciduria.
A low or absent Colorado tick fever virus IgG titer just means no exposure; it is not a measure of total IgG, so it says nothing about hypogammaglobulinemia or immunodeficiency 60.

Hypercortisolism is a real feature of the disease, but cortisol 32 hours into a prolonged corticotropin stimulation is expected to be high in anyone with responsive adrenals, so high here does not demonstrate Cushing syndrome.

Elevated C-peptide is a feature of the disease, but C-peptide rises physiologically 10 minutes after a glucose load, so high on this timepoint needs its own criteria and is not the fasting/hypoglycemic C-peptide that shows hyperinsulinism.
Elevated LH is obligate in ovarian dysgenesis, but this is the 7th specimen after an unspecified challenge, so high has no defined meaning; baseline LH is the informative measurement.

A low IgE to a meat allergen mix is the normal non-sensitised state and is not an abnormal immunoglobulin concentration; the immunoglobulin abnormality in Rosai-Dorfman disease is polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia.
Leptospira-specific IgM positivity indicates recent leptospirosis, not a raised total IgM concentration, and has no bearing on hyper-IgM syndrome.
The code is a timed sample after an unspecified challenge, so low is undefined, and hypoglycemia is a very rare (<5%), nonspecific feature of fumaric aciduria.
Hyperglycemia defines neonatal diabetes, but a glucose 30 minutes into a lactose tolerance test is expected to rise and is read against lactose-absorption criteria, not as a hyperglycemia test.

A low paper wasp IgE is the normal non-sensitised result, not an abnormal immunoglobulin concentration; the target is also an obsolete MONDO term for a serum protein polymorphism rather than a disease.
A normal wheat-specific result cannot exclude raised IgE to other plant food allergens (peanut, soy, tree nuts), and the code is a specific/total IgE ratio rather than a specific IgE level.
A low black locust pollen IgE is the normal non-sensitised result and says nothing about total immunoglobulin levels, so it has no bearing on Schimke immuno-osseous dysplasia.
A qualitative positive for Aspergillus flavus antibody shows exposure or sensitisation to that fungus, not a raised total immunoglobulin concentration.

The disease record marks hyperglycemia as explicitly NOT a feature of familial renal glucosuria (glucosuria with normal blood glucose is the point of the diagnosis), yet a positive association was emitted; the test is also a lactose tolerance timepoint.
The phenotype is annotated at 0% (excluded) in this disease but was chained as positive; in addition a low grass-pollen IgE is a normal result, not an abnormal immunoglobulin concentration.

Oxalate is a real toxic metabolite of ethylene glycol, but plasma oxalate is not an established diagnostic test for the poisoning (diagnosis rests on ethylene glycol level, osmolal and anion gaps, glycolate); the record itself cites a single case.

Antiphospholipid antibodies are a recognised risk factor found in a minority of CTEPH patients, but IgA anticardiolipin is a non-criteria isotype and the finding is occasional and shared with many thrombotic and autoimmune conditions.

ACTH is expected to rise after insulin-induced hypoglycemia, so high on this timepoint is the normal response rather than ACTH excess; ectopic ACTH secretion is also a very rare (<5%) feature of bronchial endocrine tumors.
A low glucose at 5 hours of an OGTT is reactive hypoglycemia, which is a genuine hypoglycemia, but hypoglycemia is very rare (<5%) in primary Fanconi syndrome and shared by 207 diseases.

Normetanephrine is the O-methylated metabolite of norepinephrine, not a catecholamine; it is a marker of catecholamine-secreting tumours but a high value is elevated metanephrines, not an elevated circulating catecholamine level.
A low Aspergillus terreus-specific IgE is the normal non-sensitised result and is not an abnormal circulating immunoglobulin concentration.
One minute after an IV glucose bolus is the peak of the IVGTT curve; low here is judged against glucose-disposal expectations, and a baseline or symptomatic glucose is what demonstrates hypoglycemia.

The code is for an unspecified body fluid, whereas the phenotype is defined on blood lymphocyte subsets, and it measures only the CD4 naive subset (CD45RA alone also includes non-naive cells) rather than naive T cells overall.
A single-ear, single-frequency threshold is one data point of a pure-tone audiogram; audiometry characterises the hearing loss but the specific diagnosis of DFNB100 is molecular.

A normal result on a four-tree-nut mix cannot exclude raised IgE to other foods (milk, egg, peanut, fish), so the food-allergen-level term is broader than the test covers; mixes are also less sensitive than single-allergen tests.
The record entry describes serial audiologic follow-up for progression, not diagnosis, and a single left-ear 500 Hz threshold is only one component of an audiogram; the DFNB32 diagnosis is genetic.
A low ovomucoid-specific IgE is the normal non-sensitised result and is not an abnormal circulating immunoglobulin concentration.

Audiometry is part of the clinical work-up of Usher syndrome, but one ear at one frequency is a component of the audiogram, and as the record says type 3 is defined by the course over serial tests, not by any single threshold.

The MoCA is a general cognitive screen that detects impairment of any cause; it does not distinguish Lewy body dementia from other dementias, whose diagnosis rests on core clinical features and indicative biomarkers.

MELD grades mortality risk in patients already known to have end-stage liver disease; a high score does not indicate cirrhosis (it rises with acute liver failure, kidney injury or warfarin), and the bands are waiting-list mortality strata, not diagnostic thresholds.

Breath hydrogen after lactose is the standard test, but this code is for an unspecified (XXX) challenge, so it equally covers lactulose, glucose or fructose breath tests where a rise means something else.

A normal total T3 does not exclude an abnormal T4 or free hormone level (T3 is often normal in hypothyroidism), so the term is broader than the test; the interval is also specific to the first trimester.

A high free T4 shows hyperthyroxinemia; hyperthyroidism needs a suppressed TSH and is not established in thyroiditis, exogenous thyroxine, thyroid hormone resistance or assay interference. An increased-free-T4 term fits better.
A high total/HDL cholesterol ratio is a cardiovascular risk marker, not evidence that atherosclerosis is present, and the band has no numeric bound so HIGH is undefined.

A creatinine just above the reference interval is an elevated creatinine, which can reflect muscle mass, diet, drugs or dehydration; renal insufficiency claims more than one value shows, and an elevated-creatinine term fits exactly.
The LOINC code does not specify post-bronchodilator measurement, which the phenotype and the GOLD grades require; GOLD grades also apply only when FEV1/FVC is below 0.7.

The mapping is right, but the CTCAE grade 1 band is written [75, ) with no upper bound, so as recorded a normal or raised platelet count falls in a thrombocytopenia band; the CTCAE grades also apply only to patients on cancer therapy.
An eGFR of 60-89 is GFR category G2, which is normal for many adults; stage 2 CKD additionally needs a marker of kidney damage and persistence over 3 months, as the record itself notes.

The band is built from critical (panic) limits rather than a reference interval, so counts that are clearly abnormal (2.5 or 30 x10^9/L) are called uninformative; other: the assertion is a no-information statement that carries no usable association.
